issues.span: looking ahead only the length of a yoke
issues.evidence: A yoke (a wooden bar for oxen) is an unexplained hard word; the text means they look only a short distance ahead.
issues.fix: They walk looking only a short way ahead, about as far as the wooden bar that goes across an ox's neck.

issues.span: The three are kept quiet and pure.
issues.evidence: Academic: 'the three are isolated and pure'; 'the three' is unexplained and 'kept quiet' is imprecise for 'secluded'.
issues.fix: They live apart from the crowd, and their body, speech and mind are pure.

issues.span: They have no doubts about their path.
issues.evidence: Academic: 'without doubt about their own stage' (their own level of realization), not their path.
issues.fix: They have no doubt about their own stage of practice.

issues.span: They ride in the highest, free vehicle. ... When they understand this teaching, they perfect their stored-up goodness.
issues.evidence: Academic: 'the ultimate, unattached vehicle' and the bodhisattva who realizes this Dharma; the text does not say they 'perfect' goodness by understanding, it asks what accomplished merit exceeds theirs.
issues.fix: They ride in the deepest, unattached vehicle. Anyone who understands this teaching has stored-up goodness that nothing can beat.

issues.span: An awakening hero must dedicate their goodness without any self-importance.
issues.evidence: Academic: 'A bodhisattva who dedicates without conceit will not decline' (a description, not a command).
issues.fix: An awakening hero who dedicates without any self-importance will not fall back.

issues.span: it does not mean awakening is gone
issues.evidence: Academic: 'it is not that awakening is absent' (awakening is not nonexistent), not that something present has vanished.
issues.fix: When that first thought has ended, it does not mean there is no awakening.

issues.span: By slowly building up every good quality, you perfect the quality of goodness
issues.evidence: Academic: 'by gradually perfecting virtuous qualities, one becomes a Buddha'; the children's line is redundant and tangled.
issues.fix: By slowly building up the qualities of goodness, you become a Buddha.

issues.span: They practice the things of emptiness, being without signs, and without wishes.
issues.evidence: Academic: 'the phenomena of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness'; 'the things of emptiness' is awkward for ages 8-12.
issues.fix: They practice emptiness, being without signs, and being without wishes.

issues.span: They are also not afraid of awakening. They do not think, "There is nothing here at all."
issues.evidence: Academic: 'nor do they fear awakening, thinking "There is nothing at all here"'; the thought is the cause of the fear, not something they refuse to think.
issues.fix: They are also not afraid of awakening, thinking, "There is nothing here at all."
